BARRY FLEMING.background: Attorney from Harlem (Columbia County), born May 20, 1965. B.A. (1988) and J.D. (1994) from the University of Georgia. Founding partner of Fleming Nelson, LLP; served as Hancock County attorney; formerly chaired the Columbia County Board of Commissioners. Served in the Georgia House 2003-2009 (Districts 79 and 117) and again 2013-2024 (District 121, then District 125 from January 2023). Gov. Returned in 2013. Chaired the House Judiciary Committee (2019-2020) and the committee that wrote Georgia's 2021 election law. Speaker David Ralston removed him as a committee chairman after he ran unsuccessfully for whip in 2021; he lost the 2022 race for House speaker to Jon Burns. In March 2021 the Hancock County commission voted 4-0 to ask him to resign as county attorney over HB 531, and his law practice became a target of protests after the 2021 law passed. BRAD SMITH.name: Brad Smith
BRAD SMITH.background: J. Bradley "Brad" Smith, District Attorney of the Piedmont Judicial Circuit (Banks, Barrow and Jackson counties), a Winder resident and graduate of The Citadel. A career prosecutor, he spent eight years as an assistant district attorney in the Piedmont Circuit before winning the 2008 Republican primary runoff for DA over Jefferson lawyer Donna Sikes (5,502 to 4,249, 56%), after appointed incumbent Rick Bridgeman failed to make the runoff; he took office at age 37 and was reported to be one of the youngest DAs in the state. Re-elected unopposed in 2016 and 2020 and, per Branch Politics, in November 2024.
BRAD SMITH.ideology: Elected and re-elected district attorney as a Republican. No outlet or rating placed him ideologically within the party. On winning in 2008 he said he planned to go in "quietly" and would not push major changes right away.
BRAD SMITH.record: Piedmont Circuit District Attorney since January 2009. The GBI and the Georgia attorney general's office said Smith had no knowledge of the theft scheme for which his former boss, DA Tim Madison, was imprisoned. His office prosecuted the September 2024 Apalachee High School shooting in Barrow County: on Oct. 17, 2024 he announced a 55-count indictment of 14-year-old Colt Gray (including four counts of murder) and charges against his father, Colin Gray (second-degree murder, involuntary manslaughter, cruelty to children). Colin Gray was convicted of more than two dozen felonies and on July 30, 2026 was sentenced to 15 years (prosecutors had sought 80); Colt Gray is serving life without parole. Gray's lawyers filed a motion for a new trial in August 2026.
BRAD SMITH.notes: Branch Politics lists his DA tenure start as both 2008 and 2009 (he won the 2008 election and took office the following Jan. 1). His 2024 re-election appears on the ballot as J. Bradley Smith. A 2024 Meriwether County school board race under the name Brad Smith is a different person and is listed separately. He had no website or questionnaire answers on Branch. Atlanta News First calls him 'Barrow County District Attorney'. No endorsements, finance or ratings found.

positions.stance: After winning the 2008 runoff he said he planned on "going in quietly," would not push major changes right away, and noted progress already made in restoring the office's credibility after former DA Tim Madison's theft conviction.

In announcing the 2024 Apalachee High School indictments, said the case against the shooter's father could set a precedent for holding parents legally accountable for their children's actions; at the father's trial he argued Colin Gray "was convicted for what he did know" and ignored "a substantial and unjustifiable risk."
